poc_summary: Objective: prove Dedicated can meet sustained throughput (target 1,200 QPS aggregate) with 95th latency SLOs: chat= <200ms, reranking= <150ms, embeddings= <80ms for 512-dim vectors.
Test matrix: steady load at 60% baseline, burst to 100% for 10-minute windows every hour, 12-hour soak to detect memory leaks and KV cache warmup patterns.
Representative prompts: mix of short chat (16-64 tokens), mid-length context-aware prompts (1k-4k tokens), and batch rerank requests (batch size 16).
Success criteria: sustained QPS within 10% of target for 12-hour soak, p95/p99 under thresholds, no GPU OOMs, predictable cost model demonstrated for reserved vs burst usage.
Metrics captured: per-token latency, model kernel breakdown, KV cache hit ratio, GPU utilization, tail-latency sources, billing meter traces.
Config notes: testing with quantized 8-bit model variant + memory-optimized compilation; KV cache TTL set to 30m; batching window tuned to 8-16ms.
poc_results: Initial load runs (03-08 demo): achieved 1,050 QPS sustained on 6 reserved A100-eq nodes; extrapolated 1,300 QPS with 8 nodes (linear scaling assumption).
95th latency observed: chat 180ms, rerank 140ms, embeddings 70ms under warm cache. p99 spikes correlated with cold KV-cache misses (up to 450ms).
Soak test (03-10, 12h): sustained throughput stable after 90 minutes of warm-up; KV cache hit ratio stabilized at ~88% after warm period; no memory leaks detected.

Cost projection: reserved baseline (8-node equiv) + 2x burst = est. $420k ARR when amortized w/ committed discount; Optimize recommendations suggest raising batching slightly for embeddings to cut unit cost 9%.
Open technical issues: tail-latency on cold-cache flows; temporary tokenization jitter observed for very long prompts (>6k tokens) due to fallback path in tokenizer library.
Recommended mitigations: pre-warm common prefixes during peak windows, increase cache TTL for session-based flows, enable alternative kernel selection for long-seq runs.
